sources.title: Legal Information Institute
sources.snippet: Non-profit free legal information service at Cornell Law School. The **Legal Information Institute** (**LII**) is a non-profit public service of Cornell Law School that provides no-cost access to current American and international legal research sources online. LII was established in 1992 at Cornell Law School by Peter Martin "Peter Martin (Law Professor)") and Tom Bruce with a $250,000 multi-year startup grant from the National Center for Automated Information Research. Its original mission included the intent to "carry out applied research on the use of digital information technology in the distribution of legal information,...[and t]o make law more accessible." In the early years of LII, Bruce developed Cello "Cello (web browser)") the first web browser for Microsoft Windows. LII has an extensive collection of law from the Supreme Court of the United States. The LII Supreme Court Bulletin is LII's free Supreme Court email-based subscriber and web-based publication service. "Cornell Legal Information Institute posts previews of Supreme Court cases".

facts.fact: The last amendment to the United States Constitution is Amendment XXVII, which was ratified on May 7, 1992.
Amendment XIX, which grants the right to vote regardless of sex, was passed by Congress on June 4, 1919, and ratified on August 18, 1920.
The Bill of Rights, which includes the first ten amendments to the Constitution, was ratified on December 15, 1791.

Amendment XIX, which ensures voting rights regardless of sex, was ratified on August 18, 1920. The Bill of Rights, comprising the first ten amendments, was ratified on December 15, 1791.
